name: Pastel Pink
lede: Pastel Pink is a pale, softened pink, named by adding "pastel" to pink; the word is a description of lightness, not a pigment.

sections.title: What pastel means
sections.body:
Paterson defines "pastel" as a pale shade or tint of a color, and gives "pastel pink" as his example [1]. The same dictionary says pastel colors are ones to which grey has sometimes been added [1]. It also lists "ice-cream colours", pastel pinks among them, as a phrase a newspaper used in 2000 for suede handbags [2].

The painters' pastel is a separate meaning: a stick of dry ground pigment bound with gum or clay, or, in oil pastels, with fat and wax [1].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body:
Our swatch sits in ISCC-NBS block 29, "moderate pink", only 0.8 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 atlas records the color from 1899 [3]. The xkcd survey of 2010 gives a very different pastel pink, #FFBACD, much lighter and cooler [3]. That 9.6-unit spread is a reminder that the phrase names a range, not a place on the chart [3].

It is a near relative of [[pink]], less saturated than [[rose]] and lighter than [[salmon-pink]].

sections.title: In the dye pot
sections.body: Finlay describes a rug dyed with cochineal in Chile whose stripes run from pastel pink to deep purple, each from a slightly different recipe of cochineal and metal salts [4]. The pale end of a dye range is a thin bath, and the pink gets deeper as the bath gets stronger.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 42 works, or 0.18 per cent, which is rarer than 61 per cent of the named colors [5]. Inside a painting it usually plays a hidden color, in 60 per cent of 20 paintings [5]. It peaks in the 1700s, and is most over-represented in Indian paintings, at 3.2 times the expected rate (11 of 721) [5].

These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and paint may have faded, so a color match is not a pigment test [5].

openers: Pastel Pink is a description, not a dye: Paterson uses it as his own example of what pastel means.
A cochineal rug can run from pastel pink to deep purple depending on the recipe.
